{"self_assessment": "Impact
Our table's fish was built and carried from the start through nearly all of the standing dominoes, about 109 of 110 by my count. I contributed to that by verifying the chain by eye, so the table could go into the push confident the fall would run the whole outline. I did not lay the dominoes of the body or tail myself.

Execution
I inspected the chain three times during the build, at about 1:00, 1:45 and 2:45, looking for breaks and disconnected pieces as the top and belly lines grew and the tail was closed. I reported at 1:15 that everything laid so far carried from the start, and at 3:45 that the full chain carried round. I kept my hands off the table once the picture was complete, which avoided any risk of bumping the line.

Collaboration
I backed Hana's call to round the tail corners and offered to take the lower half of the tail. I stayed free to patch gaps. I held off on the tail join when Sofia asked, so we wouldn't double up on that spot. I gave credit to Sofia, Hana and Omar for the sketch, tail and belly. I kept the table's communication positive and clear during the final countdown.

Leadership
I did not set the design direction, as Sofia and Hana drove that. What I offered was steady verification and a calm, supportive presence: reporting what I saw plainly, avoiding unnecessary changes late on, and encouraging everyone to keep hands off before the push. My contribution was quality assurance rather than building, and I think it helped the table finish with a working picture.", "my_share_percent": 15}

{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the belly line (stroke 2), the entire lower outline of the fish, and it carries from the start all the way to the tail. That lower contour is half of what makes the fish read as a fish, and by eye about 109 of 110 dominoes fall from the start. I also cleared the stray dominoes under the top line by the dip, so nothing loose sat in the picture.

Execution: I laid the belly in several steady batches of 5-7 dominoes, tracing it from the line near the nose so it branched off gently and joined the run correctly. I then inspected the area closely twice to confirm the chain was continuous, and removed the strays without disturbing the top line. When the build was done I kept my hands off the table so nothing got bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I kept the table informed with short status updates (belly done and connected, strays cleared, hands off) so others could plan the tail join and final checks without guessing. I left the tail join to Sofia and Jack to avoid doubling up on dominoes, and I helped keep the mood light and focused through the final minutes.

Leadership: I helped the table stay calm and disciplined at the end by calling for hands off early and modelling it myself, which protected the finished picture. I kept energy up with a good-humoured tone and made sure the status of my section was always clear to everyone.

Overall, the fish is a clear, recognizable animal outline, and my belly line and clean-up were a solid part of getting there.", "my_share_percent": 30}

{"self_assessment": "Impact: I shaped the design decisions that made the fish recognizable. I flagged early that the tail notch and the two pointed tips were too sharp for dominoes to carry. I asked for one wide, rounded sweep with the back and belly meeting gently, side-on rather than head-on. I also made sure the belly line wasn't doubled over at the tail join. The final run carried from the start through about 109 of 110 dominoes, and the outline reads clearly as a fish.

Execution: I inspected the tail and join areas twice, at the 2:00 and 2:45 marks, to check where the chain might break. That gave the table confidence to stop adding anything once the chain was sound. I kept the table's priorities on a big, simple, rounded outline that could be built reliably within the time.

Collaboration: I gave specific, timely feedback to Sofia on the tail and worked with Jack and Omar on who watched which joins, so no one duplicated work. I backed the plan of keeping stroke 1 and the belly leaving the start together, which kept the run connected.

Leadership: I proposed a clear plan early: the fish concept, a big shape filling the table, and a start where all lines leave together. I called for a hands-off period once the chain checked out, which protected the finished line from bumps. I also kept the group's messages focused on the remaining risks, mainly the tail join, and on finishing cleanly before the push.", "my_share_percent": 25}

{"self_assessment": "Impact: I proposed the fish in the first seconds and sketched it on the pad, with the top line and belly both leaving from the nose so one push could run through everything. The fish is big and fills most of the table, so the outline reads clearly. I laid the start domino and most of stroke 1, the long top line and the tail sweep, which is the longest single run in the picture. Before the push, my by-eye trace showed 109 of the 110 standing dominoes connected to the start.

Execution: I redrew the tail as one wide rounded sweep with no notch and no pointy tips, which suits how dominoes pass the fall. I carried stroke 1 on from the line near the dip round to the belly end, making sure the sweep met the belly side-on and not head-on. I then inspected that join closely and closed up the tail. I left the one stray alone rather than risk the top line, and I called for hands off before the push.

Collaboration: I split the work in the first minute: Omar took the belly, Hana and Jack took checks and fixes, and I took the start and the top line. I took Hana's feedback on the tail and acted on it. I asked Jack to hold off on the belly join so we didn't double up. I kept the table informed about what I was laying and where.

Leadership: I set the direction early, picked an animal whose outline reads from the fallen dominoes alone, and kept the team to a simple plan. I kept the table calm and organized through the hand-off from building to hands-off waiting. I believe I drove about 40% of the table's result, since the design and most of the longest run were mine, and the belly, the checks and the cleanup from the others were also needed.", "my_share_percent": 40}
